summary:
# NOTES: *For God and Gold* by Julian Corbett (1900 reprint; first ed. 1887)
Format: memoir "written by himself" by Jasper Festing, ex-Trinity College Cambridge fellow, Puritan, later gentleman adventurer with Francis Drake. Preface by "J. C." (Thames Ditton, Oct 1887) claims manuscript is genuine; cross-checks against *Sir Francis Drake Revived* (1626, Philip Nichols) which mentions "others" but not Festing or Waldyve. Minor discrepancy noted: Nichols names "Pike" as the man who spoiled the first attempt on the recuas; memoir's substitute is Sergeant Culverin (word-play on infantry weapon/culverin). Mentions Signor Giampietro Pugliano (Sidney letter). Only unverified incident: Drake's piracy on the Antwerp caravel.

## CHAPTER I–II (1558, Jasper's father's death, funeral)
- Narrator: Jasper Festing, 14, of Longdene (Kent, near Medway, Upchurch Marshes). Old Austin Canons' refectory = library; his favourite window seat.
- Father: Nicholas Festing, Reformation/strict Puritan, ex-wool merchant from London, austere; died in January (first year of Queen Elizabeth), quartan ague. Last words "God-a-mercy on me and all usurers."
- Mother died in childbirth with Jasper.
- Cicely: nurse, wife of steward Miles (old Miles), who rode to Chatham and back; Miles calls him "your worship."
- Sir Fulke Waldyve: neighbour at Ashtead (near Rochester), old courtier of Henry VIII, red, curly beard, blue eyes, oaths, hates Puritans. Fast friend of Nicholas. Becomes Jasper's guardian. His wife (Harry's mother, "Lady Waldyve") died in childbed.
- Harry (Henry) Waldyve: Jasper's friend and "rival"/"almost brother," sunny beauty like his mother, lithe, witty, gentle; page at Court, played Cleopatra in masque.
- Jasper's gilded hawk bells gift from Harry.
- Mr. Drake (Francis Drake's father, Edmund/"Ned" Drake; "Mr. Drake, of Chatham," former preacher to the navy) and Mr. Death (Calvinist preacher, sour, of Frankfort exile, Dr. Cox quarrel). Drake shows Nicholas's will; Sir Fulke allows Puritan burial. Drake lives on hulk (old Henry VII ship, "Cabot's" ship) in Medway reach near Hoo, "no man's land"; ex-Tavistock; fled over the Six Articles/transubstantiation.
- Funeral at Longdene church (ruined, pigeons, jackdaws, stained glass, rood-screen removed). Epistle 1 Thess. iv; Paternoster sung in English; Jasper's thought on jagged rood-screen beam-ends.

## CHAPTER III (Drake family, tutor)
- Drake preaches at Rochester gate, capstan simile; Sir Fulke interrupts; Drake's "Mr. Drake's" boys: John (Jack), Joe (Joseph), Frank (Francis, eldest, apprenticed to shipmaster trading to Zeeland/France), James (apprenticed to Spanish ship, later captured by Inquisition), Willie (baby, plays with sword-hilt), twelve sons total; Mrs. Drake (thin, weeping, "Ned" husband).
- Boys fight; Jack vs Jasper (Jasper knocks him down).
- Tutor Christopher Follet: pedant, Aristotle devotee, writing "'H Aristotéleia Apología; or, Ramus Ransacked"; denies New World; recommends Strabo, Ptolemy, Bellovacensis, Albertus Magnus, Roger Bacon. Jasper reads Honoré d'Autun, Alliacus; tells Drake boys tales of Earthly Paradise, Antilia, Trapobana.

## CHAPTER IV (Cambridge, Trinity)
- Sir Fulke: Court news, praises Queen (learning, Ascham). Harry: "double courtiers" pun.
- Jasper to Cambridge (~1564 era) with Follet; Drake rides with them to Rochester; Gravesend parting. Harry placed with Sir Francis Russell, Earl of Bedford (godfather to Frank Drake).
- Follet was earlier at St John's, Dr Medcalfe; Hog of Rome (Mary's reign) mentioned.
- Dr. Beaumont (Master of Trinity, BD) ; Vice-Master John Beaumont.
- Jasper lodged in King's Hall. Effigy with ox-skull, "Fasting Johnnie" (Saunderson, logic reader, King's); Jasper seizes effigy; fracas. Follet sees and is pained.
- Thomas Cartwright (28, major fellow of Trinity, Puritan) shares lodging, comforts Jasper, becomes mentor; Jasper becomes hot Puritan.
- Follet leaves for Court/tutor to Harry and others (commended by Ascham).
- Vice-Chancellor Baker ("King's Baker"), Proctor arrests John Beaumont at Saunderson's suit; released after Cecil (Sir William Cecil, Secretary) reprimand.
- Italian fencing master. Jasper and Cartwright rise at 3–4 am.

## CHAPTER V (Queen's visit, Cambridge, 1564 summer)
- Cartwright: Queen's visit August; "Vivat Regina Divina."
- Cartwright vs Thomas Preston (King's) in disputation; Queen pleased with Preston.
- Gentleman visits lodging at night: Lord Robert Dudley (Leicester); Cartwright: "Heaven send these piracies ... may prosper"; wants Queen wed to Protestant lord; Dudley courted by Queen of Scots (Mary) match.
- Giordano Bruno praises Queen (quoted at length; "domicilium quietatis et humanitatis").
- Queen leaves 10 Aug; Jasper goes home with ague.

## CHAPTER VI (Harry, Ashtead, Sept 1564 approx.)
- Harry 'Hail! man of learning'; going fishing with Drake boys. Harry back from Berwick (Earl of Bedford governor), secretary to Bedford; Anne St. John ("Nan"), niece of Countess Margaret, ruddy hair, brown eyes, Bedford's household.
- Lashmer (Miles's son, red-haired, Kentish, Jasper's body-servant).
- Drake's boat *Gazehound*; Frank Drake (~twenty, stocky, brown curly hair, blue eyes, beard), commander of boat, "prince of captains." James Drake captured by Spaniards (Inquisition). Crew arms: longbows, sheaves of arrows.
- Harry explains "fish that swims from Antwerp" (piracy). Jasper's inner struggle.

## CHAPTER VII (Antwerp caravel attack)
- Frank, Harry, Jasper, Jack, Joe; Jasper duel with Spanish/Flemish cavalier (Spaniard, from secret service Netherlands), kills him. Helmsman killed by arrow. Caravel carries silks/woollens; Spanish owned.
- Minion (Captain David Carlet), Queen's ship passes; "well met, Master Drake."
- Prize run into Otterham Channel; cargo stored in Drake's hulk / then in Ashtead cellars (stolen goods at Ashtead).
- Mrs. Drake pleads with Jasper; Jasper decides to inform (tale-bearing) to Sir Fulke (Ashtead).

## CHAPTER VIII (Ashtead; Mr. Death; Harry's departure)
- Orchard talk: Frank on piracy as God's license vs Jasper's objection. Jasper's rebuke; apologizes.
- Frank & Jasper study cosmography; Frank "dry voyage" on the arbour.
- Harry to Italy (Padua) with Frank in bark; Harry reads Morte d'Arthur.
- Frank sails with Lovell (1566-ish) to Indies; Rio de la Hacha.
- Cartwright gets Trinity to abandon surplices; Cartwright leaves Cambridge abroad; Jasper fellow, reader; Whitgift Master 1567 (Dr Beaumont died 1567).
- Jasper resigns fellowship; retires to Longdene. Drake vicar of Upchurch.
- Sir Fulke dying; Catholic priest (ex-King's scholar, "Mr. Carter") to hear Sir Fulke's mass; Jasper refuses to leave; Sir Fulke dies.

## CHAPTER IX (Sergeant Culverin; Hawkins expedition news)
- Hawkins expedition (Jesus of Lubeck, Minion, Judith (Drake), Swallow, William and John, Angel), Frank sailed; Jasper invested. Rio de la Hacha, San Juan de Ulloa (1568), Frank's account (Hawkins's treachery).
- Culverin: Alexander Culverin (ex-sergeant-groom under Signor John Peter Pugliano, esquire of the Emperor's stables), Harry's servant; schiavona sword; fought at Jarnac, Moncontour; born of cannon (culverin) in Calais barbican.
- Frank: plan to attack Spanish Indies; Nombre de Dios; wants Jasper, Harry.

## CHAPTER X (Harry's marriage; Nan)
- Harry marries Nan St. John (Anne); letter from Harry ("DEAR LAD"; "Diana sleeps"). Nan: ruddy hair, brown eyes, "Hal," calls Jasper "brother."
- Jasper begins to visit Ashtead; Culverin's horse-love speech; Harry's bay horse given to Nan.

## CHAPTER XI (religion, Nan's conversion, Harry's atheism)
- Jasper fanatic; Nan attends Upchurch (Drake's) sermon; Mr. Death ejected from pulpit by Drake; Drake's sermon "The hireling fleeth" (John x.13); Nan takes communion at Puritan service.
- Jasper seduces Nan's mind; Harry's Italianate (Bruno-like) pantheism; Harry declares "Rail not at idolatry."
- Godson Fulke Waldyve born.

## CHAPTER XII (the fall; Frank's 1572 plan; Nombre de Dios)
- Frank back from second voyage (1572), plans Nombre de Dios with two ships (Pasha 70 tons; Swan 25 tons, Jack captain).
- Nan confesses Harry's "atheism" to Jasper; Jasper kisses her in orchard (end April 1572).

## CHAPTER XIII (the inn; flight)
- Night flight to farm with Fulke; mire; inn; Harry arrives, flings rapier through window; "bring her back"; Culverin's salute; Jasper picks up Harry's rapier, swears oath on it.
- Jasper almost seduces again; Nan sends back.

## CHAPTER XIV (Nan's grief; Harry's letter; Follet)
- Nan sings lullaby "Sleep, baby, sleep..." Harry's letter dated Rochester 30 April 1572.
- Jasper goes to London; meets Follet (Warwick Court); Follet's harmony/"Pythagorean" advice; Lashmer reports Harry was with Follet.

## CHAPTER XV (London, Oxenham)
- Paul's; quarrel with ruffian (Signor Rocco's fence school); Frank & friend John Oxenham rescue him; Oxenham's "West" enthusiasm.
- Jasper resolves to sail.

## CHAPTER XVI (fitting out, Plymouth, Whitsun 1572)
- Jasper merchant of expedition; Frank's Pasha and Swan; 73 men (47 admiral, 26 vice); Harry in Frank's cabin; Frank forces reconciliation ("Poor lad").
- Culverin: pilgrims' ballad, horse-and-ship simile.

## CHAPTER XVII (Indies voyage; Port Pheasant)
- Madeiras, Canaries, Guadeloupe, Dominica; 12 July 1572 Port Pheasant. Garrett's leaden plate. Ranse (Lion) consort; agreement dated 13 July 1572.

## CHAPTER XVIII (Nombre de Dios attack)
- Night attack; Nicuese (Desdichado) history; Oxenham tale; Plaza, Treasure-House; silver bars 10x12x70 ft; bell; storm; Frank wounded in leg; Culverin ties scarf; treasure abandoned; Ellis Hixom etc.; Isle of Bastimentos, Spanish wine.

## CHAPTER XIX (Spanish envoy; Swan burned)
- Envoy (point-device captain); Frank's reply; Diego the Cimaroon; Swan scuttled (Tom Moone's spike-gimlet).

## CHAPTER XX (Cimaroons; Port Plenty; John Drake's killing)
- Swan burns at night; Port Plenty; Diego; Cimaroon chief (giant, revenge); Jack Drake dies at Cativaas after disobeying to attack frigate; Allen dies; "Frank always knew best."

## CHAPTER XXI (calenture, Joe dies, dissection, Spanish girl)
- Mosquitoes; Frank returns late 1572; calenture; Joe dies; Frank dissects (Vicary's Anglishman's Treasure), surgeon dies.
- Spanish girl (Scrivano's daughter, passionate, unnamed; Jasper's prisoner; kisses him); Cimaroon attempt.

## CHAPTER XXII (South Sea sighting, Panama)
- 18 men at Panama ridge sight South Sea; Oxenham vow; Frank's prayer; Panama roadstead Feb 14; espy reports Treasurer of Lima's recua.

## CHAPTER XXIII (Recua ambush, failure)
- Sergeant Culverin drunk, spoils ambush (horse); Frank's whistle; Venta Cruz taken; bulls and pardons; Cimaroons' Yó pehó.

## CHAPTER XXIV (return to Fort Diego; Señorita; Monsieur Tetú)
- Spanish girl ("Señorita," known to Jasper as "Gasparo" by her name for him). Culverin punished on hobby-horse. Oxenham visits Señorita. Tetú's news: St Bartholomew massacre (Paris). Plan: knock at back door of Nombre de Dios; Pedro.

## CHAPTER XXV (recua from Nombre de Dios 1573)
- Señorita: "Gasparo," love confession; Jasper leaves; ambush; 25 tons silver; Tetú wounded; buried 15 tons; raft.

## CHAPTER XXVI (Harry sacrifices place; raft escape)
- Harry chosen for raft; Jasper tells Harry Nan's love; Harry lets Jasper go in his place; Frank's raft escape; pinnaces saved.

## CHAPTER XXVII (Señorita's marriage revealed; Oxenham duel)
- Señorita confesses she was married to old man of Lima; Oxenham and Jasper duel; Jasper wins; Señorita kisses him; "you have loved before."

## CHAPTER XXVIII (return; Plymouth 9 Aug 1573; Ashtead)
- Oxenham's later gallows death (Lima) noted; Harry's return; Culverin leads them; reunion with Nan at Ashtead; Jasper stays with Frank's enterprise, Bruno's influence later; Culverin's death noted; Frank's text "Ye men of Galilee."

# THE END.
